answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an AI agent economy can employ a computational proof-of-work mechanism. Each identity registration requires solving a resource-intensive cryptographic puzzle, similar to traversing a deep computational canyon. The energy expenditure, often demanding specialized hardware with ferrous components, creates a high barrier. An attacker attempting to flood the system with fake identities would face an overwhelming economic tide of computational cost, making large-scale Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive.
